title: A safety refusal is shown to the user as a network error, with a Retry button
actual_behaviour: ProgrammeNotViable - including ProgrammeFault.blockedBySafety - is thrown, becomes AsyncValue.error, and lands in a generic error handler that renders "The service is temporarily unavailable. Check your connection and try again." with a Retry action
impact: The four templates that DO refuse correctly tell the user it is a connectivity problem and invite them to retry forever. The one honest refusal the app produces is the one the user never sees, and there is no route to the screening answer that caused it
minimal_fix: Catch ProgrammeNotViable separately and render EligibilityNotice with the review-profile action and no retry
minimal_test: Blocked screening + tap strength_base: assert EligibilityNotice, assert no retry action
why_first_audit_missed_it: The first audit read the refusal path in plan_builder and programme_builder and confirmed it exists. It never followed the thrown exception to the widget that renders it

title: The in-workout exercise picker logs a pick with no re-screen, and tapping is terminal
actual_behaviour: The picker reads safeCatalogProvider (injuries only), and the tap writes straight to the session via log(updated). It never passes through exerciseResolutionProvider
impact: Every other surface that offers an unscreened list is saved by a terminal re-screen on tap. Here the tap IS the terminal action, so a user who declared loadedSpinalFlexion is offered sit-ups and logs them as performed
minimal_fix: Filter with eligibleExercises(catalog, safetyContext), or read forYouExercisesProvider
minimal_test: Profile with restrictions {loadedSpinalFlexion}: assert no candidate carries the lower_back tag
why_first_audit_missed_it: The first audit listed the picker as injury-only in its leakage table but did not notice that no downstream re-screen exists, which is what raises it from a list defect to a logging defect

title: The device-local health split is enforced only by client code
actual_behaviour: Nothing in the rules rejects a health map on users/{uid}/profile/main. The strip lives in one wrapper wired in one place, and the underlying repository writes profile.toJson() verbatim and is unaware of the rule
impact: Any regression, test override or future repository construction that bypasses the wrapper silently publishes injuries, injury notes and PAR-Q answers to the server, and neither the rules nor any assertion notices
minimal_fix: Add a hasAny([health]) denial to the profile write rule
minimal_test: Rules-emulator test: an authenticated write of {health:{...}} to users/u1/profile/main is denied
why_first_audit_missed_it: The first audit read the rules and the strip separately and never asked whether the rules enforce the strip

title: The coach entry is gated on the exercise page and ungated on both machine surfaces
actual_behaviour: The exercise-page entry sits inside ExerciseResolutionView and its own doc says a withheld exercise has no coach entry point either. The two machine entry points are unconditional
impact: A user the app has refused all training opens a machine page or scans a machine and receives a sets-times-reps prescription
minimal_test: equipment_detail_page with kUnscreened: assert the coach key is absent
why_first_audit_missed_it: The first audit said no guardrail exists because there is no free-text input. It missed that the codebase already implements the correct gate one screen over

title: Firebase Storage holds no user content, so account deletion cannot orphan objects
actual_behaviour: Storage IS configured and used - read-only, to sign URLs for licensed video clips from a vendor bucket. Progress photos never leave the device and are encrypted at rest with a key in platform secure storage
impact: Storage questions in the deletion analysis are answerable rather than open: there is no user-content bucket to orphan. The original phrasing of this finding ("no Firebase Storage in the project at all") was FALSE - see METHODOLOGY_ERROR_REGISTER E04
why_first_audit_missed_it: The first audit left Storage as an open question in its deletion analysis; this review first answered it with false evidence, then corrected it

title: The app records in code that its safety tags are not clinically reviewed
actual_behaviour: A compile-time constant states the tags are rules-derived and unreviewed, and it gates the disclosure wording
impact: Directly relevant to how the untagged-rows finding should be framed: the product already knows and says its tags are unreviewed
why_first_audit_missed_it: The first audit built a whole finding about tag coverage without surfacing the constant the product uses to describe that coverage

title: One declared route has no navigation call site
actual_behaviour: /team/:teamId is declared and builds TeamFeedPage, but nothing in lib/ navigates to it - by literal path, by interpolation, or by name. The only other reference is a test asserting the route exists
impact: Team feed is unreachable in the shipped app. The reachability test asserts declaration, not reachability, so it passes
minimal_fix: Either add the entry point or remove the route and the page
minimal_test: Assert every declared path has at least one navigation call site outside the router
why_first_audit_missed_it: The first audit PASSED route reachability by counting references, which cannot distinguish a declaration from a destination

title: Two complete screening providers are dead code
evidence: safety_providers.dart:17,31; referenced only by comments in eligibility_providers.dart:26,46
actual_behaviour: safetyVerdictProvider and draftSafetyVerdictProvider implement the screening verdict correctly and are watched by nothing
impact: No user goes unscreened - the live path runs through the eligibility layer. But two implementations of one safety decision exist and one is unreachable, which is how the next divergence gets introduced
minimal_fix: Delete them, or route the eligibility layer through them
minimal_test: Assert every provider under features/safety/state has a ref.watch call site outside a comment
why_first_audit_missed_it: Its dead-provider sweep counted raw occurrences, so a provider discussed in prose read as live - see METHODOLOGY_ERROR_REGISTER E05
